title: bug: both Managed VM clients have no text for reachable vm-control codes (VERSION_MISMATCH, PROVIDER_OUTPUT_INVALID, cleanup LIFECYCLE_*/LEDGER_* errors), so they render the unknown-code fallback
description:
Found in the CQ-I06f whole-epic review at 96f7bdd4. The status provider.code comes from cli.mjs prerequisites/doctor, which can emit VERSION_MISMATCH (platform-linux.mjs:27, platform-windows.mjs:27, platform-macos.mjs:17), PROVIDER_OUTPUT_INVALID, MANIFEST_INVALID and DOCTOR_INPUT_INVALID (doctor.mjs:12-20). Cleanup errors[].code takes lifecycle.mjs REPORTABLE (:54): LIFECYCLE_*, LEDGER_*, IMAGE_IDENTITY_CHANGED, PROVIDER_OUTPUT_LIMIT, PROVIDER_INPUT_INVALID.
JetBrains MoeBundle.properties (moe.managedVm.code.*) and VS Code ManagedVm.ts CODE_TEXT (:43-56) both know only 13 codes. Everything else renders 'Refusal code X; no description' (JetBrains, MoeBundle:347) or 'Unknown code X: ...' (VS Code, ManagedVm.ts:62).
Fix: add identical text for the reachable codes in both clients, with a test per client. client-verdicts.json pins only codes, so it does not change.
definitionOfDone: Every code that vm-control status/cleanup can emit has identical actionable text in MoeBundle.properties and ManagedVm.ts CODE_TEXT.
JetBrains ManagedVmPresentationTest and VS Code managed-vm.test.cjs assert at least VERSION_MISMATCH and one cleanup LIFECYCLE_* code render their text, not the unknown fallback.
cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test (or the labelled Windows equivalent) and cd moe-vscode && npm test pass in a snapshot.

implementationPlan.description:

(a) moe-vscode/src/util/ManagedVm.ts: change ONLY the declaration `const CODE_TEXT = new Map(Object.entries({` to `export const CODE_TEXT: ReadonlyMap<string, string> = new Map(Object.entries({` (no text change yet), so the test can enumerate the client's codes. Keep the doc comment above it.
(b) moe-vscode/tests/managed-vm.test.cjs: REPLACE the one-directional test 'every JetBrains managed VM code text is the VS Code text, word for word' with a closed-world guard. reachable = the union of (1) the keys of the module-private `const MESSAGES = {...}` tables in ../../scripts/local-runner/doctor.mjs, multipass.mjs and lifecycle.mjs, parsed with /^const MESSAGES = \{\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\n\};/m then /^ {2}([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*):/gm, asserting each file yields at least one key (fail loudly, never vacuously), and (2) six literal codes, each asserted to occur as the quoted string 'CODE' in its file: PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED cli.mjs (:45), PREREQUISITES_UNAVAILABLE vm-control.mjs (:47), PROVIDER_PREREQUISITES_READY doctor.mjs (:75), VM_CONTROL_FAILED, VM_CONTROL_REPORT_TOO_LARGE and LEDGER_UNREADABLE vm-control.mjs (:24/:167/:58). Add a 2-3 line comment naming the excluded codes and why: VM_CONTROL_INPUT_INVALID exits 2 so the client shows unreadable 'failed'; VM_CONTROL_STATE_DIR_INVALID and DAEMON_* are caught inside vm-control (VM_CONTROL_FAILED, or a preserve reason); CLI_INPUT_INVALID, NATIVE_SMOKE_* and CERTIFY_* belong to cli.mjs commands vm-control never runs. Assert: the sorted JetBrains bundle codes (/^moe\.managedVm\.code\.([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/gm, text trimEnd) deepEqual sorted reachable; the sorted uppercase keys of M.CODE_TEXT deepEqual sorted reachable; and for every reachable code M.readiness(run('status', status({ provider: { ready: false, code } })))[0] === `VM provider: not ready. ${bundleText}` (message = code).
(c) Add test 'V5: VERSION_MISMATCH and cleanup lifecycle and ledger codes render their own text, not the unknown fallback' with EXACT strings from step 2: readiness for provider { ready: false, code: 'VERSION_MISMATCH' } -> 'VM provider: not ready. ' + VERSION_MISMATCH text; M.notes(run('cleanup', cleanup({ errors: [{ instance: D, code: 'LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER' }, { instance: E, code: 'LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED' }] }))) deepEqual [`${D}: not deleted. ` + LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER text, `${E}: not deleted. ` + LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED text].
(d) moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/ManagedVmPresentationTest.kt: add `P6 producer codes render their own text and the bundle codes are exactly KNOWN_CODES`: load MoeBundle.properties with Properties exactly as the existing bundle test does; assertEquals(ManagedVmPresentation.KNOWN_CODES, the set of bundle keys matching moe.managedVm.code.[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]* with the prefix stripped); assertEquals(text(K.PROVIDER_NOT_READY, code("VERSION_MISMATCH")), readiness(status(provider = """{"ready":false,"code":"VERSION_MISMATCH"}"""))[0]); assertEquals(listOf(text(K.CLEANUP_ERROR, d, code("LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER")), text(K.CLEANUP_ERROR, e, code("LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED"))), notes(decode(CLEANUP, <cleanup line with those two errors>))); then render those three with a local resolver (MessageFormat(bundle.getProperty(key), Locale.ROOT).format(args, nested ManagedVmText resolved first, like resolve() at ManagedVmPanel.kt:30; build the array with arrayOf<Any>/toTypedArray<Any>, the Kotlin intersection-type gotcha) and assertEquals the same exact full strings as V5. Do not call MoeBundle.message in the unit test.
Run `cd /mnt/d/projexts/moes/moe-vscode && node --test tests/managed-vm.test.cjs` in place (allowed: it builds and installs nothing) and record the RED in the step note: 17 codes missing from both clients and V5 rendering 'Unknown code VERSION_MISMATCH: ...'. A JetBrains RED run is optional (it needs the lease).

implementationPlan.description:
Minimum implementation (GREEN). Add the same 17 texts, byte-identical, in the same order, in three places:
- moe-vscode/src/util/ManagedVm.ts CODE_TEXT: after LIFECYCLE_STATE_UNKNOWN, before the four lowercase reasons.
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties: one line moe.managedVm.code.<CODE>=<text> each, right after moe.managedVm.code.LIFECYCLE_STATE_UNKNOWN (:385).
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/ManagedVmPresentation.kt KNOWN_CODES (:89-93). This is required: refusal() (:159) gates on KNOWN_CODES, so bundle text alone would stay unused.
Error handling stays as it is and fails closed: an unknown or malformed code still renders the fixed unknown-code fallback (refusal() / codeText()), a malformed report stays unreadable, and producer text, paths or stderr never reach the UI. This step only widens the known-code tables.
Texts (ASCII only; no apostrophe, <, >, braces, & or backtick, so the existing bundle test and MessageFormat stay safe; no trailing spaces; already validated):
MANIFEST_INVALID=The bundled Multipass provider manifest is missing or invalid; reinstall Moe.
VERSION_MISMATCH=The Multipass client and daemon versions differ; restart Multipass, or reinstall it, so both run the same approved version.
PROVIDER_OUTPUT_INVALID=Multipass returned output Moe could not read; install an approved Multipass version, then refresh.
DOCTOR_INPUT_INVALID=Moe called the prerequisite check with invalid options; update or reinstall Moe.
PROVIDER_COMMAND_FAILED=A Multipass command failed; check that the Multipass service is running, then refresh.
PROVIDER_OUTPUT_LIMIT=Multipass output was larger than Moe accepts; check the Multipass installation, then refresh.
PROVIDER_INPUT_INVALID=The Multipass executable path was empty or invalid, so Multipass was not run; update or reinstall Moe.
LIFECYCLE_INPUT_INVALID=Moe passed invalid input to the VM lifecycle, so nothing was changed; update or reinstall Moe.
LIFECYCLE_NAME_COLLISION=A VM that Moe did not launch already held this reserved name, so Moe leaves it untouched; remove it in Multipass only if it is yours.
LIFECYCLE_RETRY_EXHAUSTED=Every allowed launch try for this VM failed; reconcile, then clean up.
LIFECYCLE_NOT_OWNER=This VM record belongs to another task attempt, so Moe left it untouched; reconcile, then refresh.
LIFECYCLE_PHASE_INVALID=The VM record is in a phase that does not allow this action; reconcile, then try again.
LEDGER_INPUT_INVALID=Its ledger update was invalid and was not written; the VM may already be gone. Reconcile, then clean up again.
LEDGER_RECORD_INVALID=Its ledger record is missing or unreadable; the VM may already be gone. Reconcile, then clean up again.
LEDGER_CONFLICT=Its ledger record changed during the update; the VM may already be gone. Reconcile, then clean up again.
LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED=Its ledger record could not be written; the VM may already be gone. Check free space and permissions under ~/.moe/runner-state (or MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR), then clean up again.
IMAGE_IDENTITY_CHANGED=The VM image no longer matches its recorded identity; Moe never overwrites it, so new image evidence is required.
The LEDGER_* wording is deliberate: a per-record LEDGER_* cleanup error only comes from ledger.update after purgeOwned has verified the VM absent (lifecycle.mjs:361-369), so the 'not deleted' row must not imply the VM is still there. Change a text only to fix a provable inaccuracy, and then identically in both clients and in V5/P6. The existing 13 code texts and the 4 reason texts stay byte-for-byte. Re-run `cd /mnt/d/projexts/moes/moe-vscode && node --test tests/managed-vm.test.cjs` and record GREEN.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN: node --test tests/managed-vm.test.cjs shows 11 pass and 0 fail. I added the 17 identical texts to ManagedVm.ts, MoeBundle.properties and KNOWN_CODES. The diff for the 5 files is +97/-4, additions only apart from the export line and the KNOWN_CODES trailing comma. The new lines contain no non-ASCII, ampersand or apostrophe.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (a) Only add the 17 texts. Rejected on its own: the root cause is client code lists drifting from the producer. A closed-world guard is about 15 test lines and turns the next producer code into a red test, not a silent fallback. (b) Export the code tables from scripts/local-runner. Rejected: it widens scope into the bundled producer, which other owners edit. The test parses the module-private MESSAGES tables instead, and fails loudly if a table moves. (c) Put the producer guard in the Kotlin test too. Rejected: the JetBrains snapshot archives only moe-jetbrains. Transitivity covers it: KNOWN_CODES == bundle (P6) and bundle == producer set == CODE_TEXT (VS Code guard). (d) Per-client wording ('reinstall the plugin' vs 'the extension'). Rejected: code texts must be identical, so 'reinstall Moe'.

Both clients know 13 today; 17 are missing, prototyped in a scratch copy at baseline baa704f5. JetBrains renders through KNOWN_CODES plus bundle keys. VS Code CODE_TEXT is a Map holding both the codes and the 4 lowercase preserve reasons, so filter /^[A-Z]/ when enumerating. The VS Code test loads ManagedVm.ts via ts.transpileModule plus vm.runInThisContext, so an exported Map is a real Map (instanceof checked in the prototype). Both MoeBundle.properties and the .mjs files are eol=lf; the regexes still accept CRLF.
